title: Retro game and application discovery
summary: Screen Amiga and Atari ST sources: add 16 projects.
notes: Personally screened hundreds of repository results against current main, focusing on Amiga and Atari ST games and applications. Reviewed pinned repository trees, documentation and selected source. Original source releases, reverse-engineered reimplementations and independent remakes are identified separately. No binaries or installers executed. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Official Acid Software Blitz BASIC 2 source archive, rescued from Simon Armstrong’s 1994–95 Amiga hard disk. Includes assembler source, examples and development materials.
Modified Blitz BASIC 2 and TED sources with small compiler optimizations and compile-and-quit support, derived from the published Blitz 2.15 source.

Maintained 68k AMOS Professional source based on the Aminet source archive, with build fixes, editor and memory changes. The author distinguishes its history from the independently re-uploaded official repository.
Source archive of Alain Malek’s Action Replay-like Amiga monitor, supporting memory inspection, disassembly and editing while a game or demo has control.
Original Twintris source released by programmer Svein Berge with permission described in the repository, including separate main-game and menu source images.
Reverse engineering of Tim Follin’s Atari ST YM sound driver, with a buildable driver listing, simple wrapper and data reader.
Repository-wide collection of WHDLoad game and application install sources, including slaves and disk-imaging support. These are compatibility patches rather than recovered full game sources.
C++ animation and video codec library including Amiga ANIM/CDXL, Atari SEQ and DOS-era formats. The author documents cross-checking against FFmpeg and other references.
C#/MonoGame remake of the Polish Amiga RPG Legion based on original AMOS source supplied by its authors. Described as playable beta with missing music and other gaps.
Modula-2 and SDL2 port/recreation informed by the released original Amiga C and 68k source. Author reports incomplete saving, placeholder effects and no full unassisted playthrough.

Rust/SDL3 port of the 1987 Amiga game, developed from research documentation and subsystem specifications. The author describes it as an agentic-development learning project and does not promise releases.
Original Gribnif Software source for MemFile 3, an Atari ST memory, file and disk-sector editor. Includes GEM resources and historical documentation.
Gribnif’s original scriptable Atari ST application installer source, including code and GEM resources.
Original Gribnif cookie-jar manager and accompanying Atari ST test source, designed to create or enlarge the system’s shared cookie jar.
Gribnif’s original World Clock desk accessory/application, including GEM resources, map data and C source.
Gribnif’s original small programmer’s calculator for Atari ST, with C and assembly source and configuration data.
